Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) involves motor neuron degeneration driven by survival of motor neuron (SMN) protein deficiency.
Disease-modifying therapies have improved SMA outcomes while unmasking a complex spectrum of residual disease biology.

The findings extend the concept of selective vulnerability past motor neurons to peripheral immune cells.
The commentary poses the critical therapeutic question: What constitutes adequate SMN restoration?
Treatment-modified SMA is shaped by cell type, developmental timing, SMN requirement, and downstream response, impacting systemic versus CNS-directed therapies.
